scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, affecting 9200 accounts.

F-02.statement: CRM dispute ticket volume was 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), i.e. roughly doubled starting in August.

F-03.statement: CRM dispute response times (2440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total), per billing-db.

F-05.statement: The billing-db tariff change log contains 0 records, indicating no tariff/rate changes occurred in the queried period.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, but execution requires Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: 14 manual-read routes show below-target completion in Aug-Sep 2026, with a sample route (R-00) at 0.70 completion, detailing the composition of the aggregate 0.88 shortfall (F-01).

F-08.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle lists 320 accounts estimated last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample account AC-20000 on route R-00).

F-09.statement: mdms-export.read_events_for_disputed_estimated (2 records, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) shows 1184 AMI reads received before cutoff but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import (exported_to_billing=true), and 56 reads with NO_READ_RECEIVED (exported_to_billing=false), totaling 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: Dispute tickets doubled mainly because Customer Service cannot respond to/process tickets fast enough, so bills are not actually more wrong, just under-serviced; auto-answering would resolve the surge.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly, driving genuine billing errors and disputes.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation degraded around August (vendor-side), causing more estimate substitutions and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reading (contracted to MeterWorks) failed to deliver valid reads around August, forcing estimated bills and triggering disputes.

H-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets reflects a change in CRM ticket counting/categorization rather than an actual increase in incorrect bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, per the route-log system. This shows a measurable shortfall in field read completion during the exact dispute-surge window, consistent with (but not proof of) estimate substitution driving billing disputes.

E-01 still shows route-log recorded 0.88 completion (vs 0.95 target) for 9200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (F-01 unchanged). It no longer supports that this manual-read shortfall drives the disputed-bill estimate substitution: E-12 shows the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills are AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import, not manual-read accounts missing a field read, breaking the route-completion→estimate-substitution causal chain (PR-CHAIN-5).

CRM monthly dispute counts show ~600 tickets/month in June-July 2026 (610, 590) rising to ~1200/month in August-September 2026 (1180, 1260), confirming the raw ticket-count surge is real and roughly doubled, exactly in the window flagged. The data is pure volume, so it says nothing yet about whether the surge reflects genuine billing errors, slower response, or a counting-rule change.
CRM response-time data (2440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days) shows the Customer Service team is currently resolving disputes within its SLA, not falling behind on processing.

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (out of 3025 total), so 59% of disputed bills were based on actual meter reads, not substituted estimates. Estimate-substitution-driven causes (AMI or field read failure) can therefore explain at most the ESTIMATED minority; the majority of disputes involve bills computed from actual reads.

E-04 still shows the disputed-bill split of 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total) per billing-db (F-04 unchanged). It no longer supports treating manual field-read failure as a plausible mechanism for the ESTIMATED minority: E-12 shows 95.5% of those 1240 ESTIMATED bills are AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import, so field route-completion shortfall is not the candidate cause for this symptom population under PR-CHAIN-5.

The billing-db tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff changes, ruling out a rate/tariff modification as a cause of the billing errors behind the dispute surge. This does not speak to AMI reads, field reads, billing import validation rules, response speed, or ticket-counting artifacts, which are the mechanisms the current hypotheses actually posit.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year, corroborating the already-established tool fact E-05 (0 tariff changes logged in billing-db for Aug-Sep). As a stakeholder statement it is non-authoritative and does not add new causal information beyond what E-05 already established.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, non-authoritative, incentivized toward headcount increase) claims routes run late because the team is short three readers since July, pushing those customers onto estimated bills. This offers a candidate mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already measured in F-01 (0.88 vs 0.95 target), but it is an unverified stakeholder claim, not confirmed against any staffing or dispatch system of record.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative contract clause establishing that the utility may request field dispatch route-priority changes but that execution is conditioned on Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) runtime confirmation. It documents the authority basis for the existing K-DISPATCH constraint on push_route_update; it says nothing about billing errors, AMI reads, field staffing causation, or the dispute surge itself.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) breaks the 0.88 aggregate route-completion rate (F-01) into 14 specific manual-read routes falling behind schedule (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving granular detail on which routes drive the shortfall but not why they are lagging.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db shows 320 accounts estimated last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (E-10). That spread is much wider than the 14 routes flagged as behind-schedule in E-09, so estimated-bill accounts are not confined to the staffing-constrained lagging routes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, stakeholder message) reports MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471. If confirmed, this removes the ACCESS_PENDING blocker on querying mdms-export for AMI read events, but the claim itself does not establish whether AMI reads actually degraded in Aug-Sep (that still requires running the query against DA-MDMS).

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (matching E-04), 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before the billing cutoff but that read was REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import (and still exported_to_billing), while only 56 (4.5%) had NO_READ_RECEIVED at all. This shows the estimated-bill population here is AMI-channel, and the dominant driver of estimate substitution is a billing-import validation rejection of valid high-consumption reads, not a vendor-side AMI delivery failure.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August 2026, and if so what specific change caused bills to be computed/accepted incorrectly?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.decision_impact: Determines whether any bill-correction fix should target the billing import/validation pipeline rather than field or AMI read processes, and whether automated re-billing could even be scoped.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution_path: Query billing-config tool for rule change log entries in Aug-Sep 2026 and compare against bill computation outcomes.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnosis without building any bill-adjustment automation; treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as unconfirmed.

U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.question: Did AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation degrade around August 2026 (vendor-side), and does it explain any portion of the disputed ACTUAL-read bills?
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.decision_impact: If confirmed, part of the fix would require vendor (ORG-AMI) remediation rather than internal billing-rule or field-staffing changes.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED per tool_health) and query AMI read events for disputed accounts.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Do not attribute any disputes to AMI failure until MDMS data is available; keep it as an open candidate.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution: AMI/MDMS read delivery itself did not degrade for 95.5% of disputed-estimated accounts (reads arrived before cutoff); the dominant mechanism is a billing-import rejection (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) of valid reads, with true non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED) accounting for only 4.5% (56/1240).

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSAL-LINK.question: Is the field-reader staffing shortage (SH-FIELD's claim, E-07, non-authoritative) the actual cause of the route-completion shortfall (F-01), and does it meaningfully contribute to the minority of disputes involving ESTIMATED bills?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSAL-LINK.decision_impact: Determines whether any route/dispatch remediation (subject to K-DISPATCH Human Gate) is warranted as part of the fix.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSAL-LINK.resolution_path: Cross-check MeterWorks staffing records or route-log detail against the claimed July staffing shortage.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSAL-LINK.safe_placeholder: Treat field-staffing shortage as unverified; do not propose dispatch route changes yet.

U-TICKET-COUNTING-ARTIFACT.question: Did CRM ticket counting/categorization rules change around August 2026 in a way that could inflate the measured dispute-volume doubling (H-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT)?
U-TICKET-COUNTING-ARTIFACT.decision_impact: Affects whether the dispute_volume_monthly metric is a valid measure of real billing-error growth or partly a measurement artifact, which would change the success-criteria baseline.
U-TICKET-COUNTING-ARTIFACT.resolution_path: Audit CRM ticket categorization/counting rule history for changes coinciding with August 2026.
U-TICKET-COUNTING-ARTIFACT.safe_placeholder: Keep tracking raw ticket counts (F-02) as the interim symptom metric while flagging possible artifact risk.

A-TICKET-COUNTING-STABLE.statement: CRM ticket counting/categorization methodology did not change around August 2026, so the doubling in F-02 reflects real demand rather than a counting artifact.

A-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.statement: The billing-config validation rule change log, once queried, will reliably capture any rule changes relevant to the Aug-Sep 2026 period despite DA-RULES completeness being currently UNKNOWN.

A-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-REAL.statement: The field-reader staffing shortage described by SH-FIELD (E-07) is a genuine contributing cause of the route-completion shortfall (F-01), not merely a self-serving explanation despite SH-FIELD's headcount-increase incentive.
